newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close lower after dollar correction.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close lower after dollar correction.

text.p: French stocks gave up their early gains on Tuesday and closed lower after the dollar slipped from its highs, spurring profit-taking in the French market.
"The dollar slipped back abruptly, falling below 1.70 German marks," said a dealer. Other traders said the bourse was ripe for profit-taking after hitting all-time highs in early trading.
"Some people may also be a bit nervous ahead of the U.S. CPI (consumer price index) due out tomorrow," another dealer said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 16.96 points, or 0.64 percent, at 2,617.52 after retreating from a historic high of 2,658.62 hit early in the session.
The dollar corrected in European trading on Tuesday against the mark, which was bolstered by the lira's weakness on concerns Italy may not make the first round of European monetary union.
The French CAC-40 futures contract settled at 2,619 points on Tuesday, down 29 points.
Volume was a heavy 10.5 billion francs.

Shares in tyremaker Michelin surged against the trend, finishing up 4.18 percent at 351.30 francs, after investors were drawn by the previous day's weakness in the stock after the company said it would redeem 3.5 billion francs of convertible bonds ahead of schedule.

Shares in steelmaker Usinor closed up 3.2 percent at 87.20 francs after the company reduced its dividend by less than anticipated after reporting a big drop in 1996 net attributable profit to 1.49 billion francs from a record 4.43 billion in 1995.
